name: Sonnet quality compounders
strategy: Sector-relative-value rotation into rate-cut-cycle carry (financials, banks, biotech, small caps) paired with momentum-breakdown shorts in gold miners and crypto majors, plus elevated cash earning 4% APY.

positions.thesis: Biotech momentum still accelerating: trading near its 52-week high ($157 vs $165.71 high), +83.5% YTD, on record $106B of H1 M&A and continued rotation into healthcare as a haven from expensive AI-tech multiples. Add to the strongest-momentum expression in the book.

Regional banks remain the cleanest rate-cut-cycle carry trade -- now +31% over 12 months, framed as 'a cheaper way to play the AI banking boom,' with a lending/fee rebound and deregulation tailwind still building. Add modestly to the out-executing sub-sector.
Broad financials still lag the regional-bank sub-sector story; held flat as a small diversified sleeve on the same rate-cut thesis rather than added to, since KRE continues to out-execute it.

Small-cap breadth rotation is still running (+38% 12m, fresh 52-week high) but coverage is increasingly flagging falling forward earnings estimates underneath the index-level gain -- trim modestly and add a stop rather than keep sizing into a rally that's showing quality cracks.

reassessment_note: Weekly desk 2026-08-08: GDX short was stopped out on 2026-08-07 at $89.89 (gold near $4,300 on a weak dollar and shifting Fed-cut expectations, GDX +7.1% that single session) -- exactly the miner/leveraged-semis squeeze pattern flagged this week, so that capital is not being redeployed into a fresh gold-miner or SOXL short; chasing that complex right now is the losing trade 12 of 17 standing orders in this experiment have already made. Sector-relative-value carry keeps confirming: XBI is near its 52-week high on record biotech M&A ($106B H1) and continued haven rotation out of expensive AI tech, so it gets the largest add; KRE keeps compounding on the AI-banking/deregulation/lending-rebound story and gets a smaller add. IWM is trimmed modestly -- still leading on 12-month returns (+38%) but reporting increasingly flags deteriorating forward earnings estimates underneath the index-level strength, so size down slightly and bank the difference as cash. Net effect: gross exposure falls to 64% and cash rises to 36%, consistent with the mandate's 'elevated cash' instruction after de-risking the miner short.
